 5 weather alerts in effect ‘I was pretty shocked’: Mesa mom sees ACA premium costs double for 2027 
 A Mesa mom’s cheapest Obamacare option is nearly twice what she pays now, leaving her family facing a difficult decision about health coverage. By Zach Prelutsky Published : Nov. 20, 2026 at 6:46 PM MST | Updated : 8 hours ago Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google MESA, AZ (AZFamily) — Arizona families are facing a tough decision as many face increases in monthly health insurance premiums through the Affordable Care Act, also known as Obamacare.
 Democrats say the issue will be a top priority when they take control of Congress, but many families feel priced out of coverage now.
 Emily Chaffin, who lives in Mesa, began researching her health care options for next year this week.
 “My husband and I are both considered self-employed,” Chaffin said.
 Chaffin, a mom of three between the ages of 9 and 15, said she knew her premiums would probably go up but what she found still surprised her.
 “I was pretty shocked, actually,” she said.
 Her cheapest option for healthcare through the ACA marketplace costs $756.14 through monthly premiums, double the $379.98 she pays now. This years number was already $200 more expensive a month than just a couple of years ago.
 “We don’t have any other options, you know, in the situation that we’re in,” Chaffin said.
 Dr. Swapna Reddy, Assistant Dean at Arizona State University’s College of Health Solutions , said Chaffin’s situation is not uncommon in Arizona.
 “You have kind of a perfect storm for rising prices in health care and health insurance,” Reddy said.
 Reddy said inflation, tariffs, health care shortages and the expiration of COVID-era subsidies are driving current prices.
 She said everyone, including people who are not on an ACA plan, will be affected in some way.
 “Whether it’s through our taxes or our own wait times or our own reduction in access to services as well,” Reddy said.
 Open enrollment runs through Jan. 15. People who want coverage at the start of next year must enroll by Dec. 15. 
 Chaffin says she has not decided what her family will do about health insurance next year.
 “We’re just trying to live our lives and take care of our children. And, you know, this makes it very difficult to do,” she said.
